sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emily.
I am happy you are here.
Today we will talk about Kyrgyzstan.
Kyrgyzstan is a mountainous, peaceful,
and traditional country in Central Asia.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Kyrgyzstan?
Kyrgyzstan is in Central Asia.
It is next to Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, and China.
It has no sea, but it has many mountains, lakes, and valleys.
What is the capital city of Kyrgyzstan?
The capital city is Bishkek.
It is a green city with parks, markets, and mountain views.
It is the largest city in the country.
Other cities include Osh, one of the oldest cities in Central Asia.
Karakol, near Lake Isekul, Jalalabad, and Takmak.
How many people live in Kyrgyzstan?
About 7 million people live in Kyrgyzstan.
Most people live in cities, valleys, and villages.
The people are called Kyrgyz, and they are known for their hospitality and love of nature.
What language do people speak in Kyrgyzstan?
The official language is Kyrgyz.
Russian is also widely spoken, especially in cities.
Some people also speak Uzbek, English, or Chinese.
Many people are bilingual.
What is the weather like in Kyrgyzstan?
Kyrgyzstan has a continental climate.
Hot summers, cold winters, with snow in the mountains.
In the mountains, it is cool, even in summer.
In the valleys, summers are warm and dry.
What does Kyrgyzstan look like?
Kyrgyzstan has tall mountains, about 90% of the country is mountains,
green valleys and meadows, beautiful lakes like Isekul,
the second largest mountain lake in the world.
Forest, rivers, and glaciers.
It is a perfect place for hiking, horse riding, and camping.
What animals live in Kyrgyzstan?
In the wild, you may see snow leopards, wolves, and eagles,
yaks, deer, and foxes, horses, sheep, and goats on farms.
The Golden Eagle is a symbol of the country.
Many people love eagle hunting as a traditional sport.
What do people eat in Kyrgyzstan?
Kyrgyz food is hearty, warm, and meat-based.
People eat lamb, beef, and horse meat, rice, noodles, and bread,
dairy products like yogurt, cream, and cheese.
Popular dishes,
bech barmock, boiled meat with flat noodles, the national dish,
plav, rice with meat and carrots,
lagmen, hand-pulled noodles with meat and vegetables,
samsa, baked pastry with meat,
or sock, fried dough pieces, often served with tea.
What do people drink in Kyrgyzstan?
People drink tea. Black tea is very common.
Kimmies fermented mares milk.
Iron, a salty yogurt drink.
Water, fruit juice, and coffee.
Tea is served many times a day, often with bread or snacks.
What is life like in Kyrgyzstan?
Life in Kyrgyzstan is a mix of modern cities and traditional village life.
People enjoy family gatherings, visiting nature, horse riding in festivals,
playing music and telling stories,
living in yurts during summer in the mountains.
The yurt is a round tent made of felt.
It is an important symbol of Kyrgyz culture.
What are some holidays and traditions in Kyrgyzstan?
Now, ruse, March 21st, the spring new year.
Independence Day, August 31st,
Victory Day, May 9,
Eid al-Feder and Eid al-Ada Muslim holidays.
During festivals, people wear traditional clothes,
cook special meals, and play horse games like cockboru.
Some fun facts about Kyrgyzstan.
The flag is read with a sun and a yurt roof in the center.
People love to recite the epic of manas, a long heroic poem.
The name Kyrgyz, may mean 40 tribes.
Horses are very important in daily life and celebrations.
Lake Isik cool never freezes, even in winter.
Now you know many things about Kyrgyzstan.
You know where it is, what people eat and how they live.
You learned about nature, culture, and traditions.
Great job.
Or as they say in Kyrgyz,
Kosh Bolunas.
